correctness.rationale: Binary addition n+2n proves t=2s2(n)-s2(3n) is a carry count, excludes t=1, and bounds 0<=t<=r. A digit-length extremal argument forces t=0 whenever s2(3n)>r. In the t=0 case no adjacent ones occur; in the t>=2 case explicit exact binary identities for (10)^h1^b and 1^t(01)^h realize all parity-compatible b,t with matching sharp lower lengths. Direct parity-square count gives binomial(r,2)+2. Enumerations through r=15 and 2401 witnesses independently corroborate the algebra; r=1 and n=0 are included.

value.rationale: The first nontrivial odd binary dilation n->3n yields a natural two-coordinate weight and central-binomial valuation invariant. The theorem classifies support and shortest bit lengths for every dyadic interval, exposing a rigid forbidden single-carry layer and a quadratic support size. Known marginal values or 3-flimsy sign statistics do not answer this complete support question. The result does not depend on a proposed downstream conjecture or arbitrary finite cutoff.
